verdict.rationale: Vercel's own pricing docs publish a per-unit on-demand rate table. It covers Fast Data Transfer (bandwidth) at $0.15/GB, origin transfer, CDN requests and CPU duration, and states that per-unit charges begin once included amounts or credit are used. Function Active CPU and Provisioned Memory rates are referenced on a separate per-region pricing page. The story names three meters, but the evidence explicitly prices only bandwidth; invocations are covered only indirectly through compute rates, and build minutes not at all. Missing for 10: an explicit per-invocation overage rate, a build-minute overage rate, and independent corroboration of the fee schedule.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I know the exact overage fee schedule for exceeding plan usage limits (bandwidth, invocations, build minutes) before I get billed

citations.quote: Fast Data Transfer: First 100 GB / Flat Rate CDN / $0.15 per 1 GB
Once you pass an included amount or use your credit, Vercel charges per unit of usage.
You are only billed during actual code execution and not during I/O operations
The Pro plan is billed monthly based on the number of deploying team seats, paid add-ons, and any on-demand usage during the billing period.
